verses.english: “Reverend, they speak of one ‘freed both ways’.

verses.pali: Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, ubhatobhāgavimutto vutto bhagavatā”ti?
verses.english: What is the one freed both ways that the Buddha spoke of?”

verses.pali: “Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: “First, take a mendicant who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … enters and remains in the first absorption.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya ca naṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way. And they understand that with wisdom.

verses.pali: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ubhatobhāgavimutto vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena …pe….
verses.english: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the one freed both ways in a qualified sense. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
verses.english: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya ca naṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way. And they understand that with wisdom.

verses.pali: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ubhatobhāgavimutto vutto bhagavatā nippariyāyenā”ti.
verses.english: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the one freed both ways in a definitive sense.”
